A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LINO-UniPS and PS-Verse. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated results.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark evaluations, PS-Verse experiments, architectural ablations, and real-image reconstructions.

after.justification: V3 retains original normal-reconstruction experiments and adds PBR material prediction, model-size comparisons, and mobile-phone reconstruction examples.

M1.justification: The core register-token, interleaved-attention, wavelet, and normal-gradient framework remains. V3 adds a joint PBR variant predicting albedo, metallic, and roughness alongside normals, with additional weighted MSE losses (Appendix A1.2). Its reported lighting-supervision vectors also gain distance-to-camera coordinates (A1.1.3). Curriculum training and the three lighting-token types already existed in v1.

E1.justification: V3 substantially extends task coverage from normal estimation to joint PBR material prediction on PS-Verse, and adds evaluation on its own mobile-phone captures (A1.2 and A1.5.2). DiLiGenT, LUCES, DiLiGenT102, and the near-planar failure examples remain; DiLiGenT102 is relocated to the appendix rather than removed.

E2.justification: The dataset ablation replaces SDM-UniPS trained on PS-Mix/PS-Verse with UniMS-PS trained on its native dataset, PS-Mix, and PS-Verse (v1 Table 3; v3 Table 2). V3 also adds UniMS-PS to the PS-Mix architectural comparison and introduces IDArb and the BRDF-capable SDM-UniPS variant in PBR evaluation. Conversely, UniMS-PS disappears from Figure 1's qualitative comparison.

E3.justification: PS-Verse evaluation changes from 50 scenes, ten per complexity level, to 441 held-out single-object scenes. Reported PS-Mix training changes from approximately 140 to 100 epochs. V3 introduces smaller-model controls and timing protocols, plus PBR fine-tuning and material-map PSNR/SSIM evaluation. Figure 1 replaces thresholded angular accuracy with inverse MAE. These are reported protocol changes, without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V3 adds an explicit curriculum-learning ablation and two smaller-model comparisons testing whether gains depend on parameter count (Tables 2 and 6). It revises lighting-token attention analysis. However, it removes the per-complexity ablation breakdown and sparse-input tests at K=3/6 on LUCES and K=4/8 on DiLiGenT. The MLP-decoder analysis and near-planar failure case remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed identities, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Feature-variance visualizations and the DiLiGenT102 mean/median summaries are retained; these do not establish uncertainty estimates across experimental runs.

E6.justification: Reported full-input MAEs change from 4.74 to 4.65 on DiLiGenT and 9.48 to 9.43 on LUCES; UniMS-PS changes from 4.97 to 5.01 and 11.10 to 11.21, respectively. LUCES K=15 worsens from 9.59 to 9.94. V3 adds curriculum, capacity/timing, and PBR results, including albedo PSNR 30.49 in Table A1, while removing several breakdowns. Altered experimental descriptions prevent unqualified same-protocol improvement claims. The DiLiGenT102 heatmap is identical and relocated.

T1.justification: Appendix A1.2 adds a formal joint PBR objective and adaptive material-loss weights; A1.1.3 revises the lighting-vector definitions to include distance. Existing normal-loss and fusion mathematics remain substantially unchanged, with no new theorem or proof. The new PBR weights have an indexing inconsistency: the objective uses lambda6–lambda8, while their definitions use lambda1–lambda3.

C1.justification: The central decoupling, detail-recovery, and PS-Verse contributions remain. V3 strengthens the main benchmark claim from winning the most DiLiGenT objects to winning every object except Ball on both benchmarks (Section 4.2). Figure 1 instead narrows the scanner comparison from exceeding a professional scanner to visually rivaling one.

C2.justification: V3 adds interpretations that architectural gains persist at comparable parameter counts, that simple MLP decoders suit Ball objects, and that PBR baseline artifacts reflect incomplete disentanglement. Directional-token attention is now interpreted as broad and low-frequency, contrasting with v1's localized area-token interpretation. The computational-cost and near-planar normal-inversion limitations are retained.

D1.justification: V3 adds PBR fine-tuning, output-channel, loss-weight, and model-size information, and revises training resources from eight H100s for seven days to two for three days. It omits v1's explicit DINOv2-small pretrained initialization, 40K-scene training subset, rendering bit depth, and light-count details. These omissions do not establish training from scratch or use of all 100K scenes. Project/code/model/demo link targets remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds IDArb (Li et al., 2025) for the PBR comparison and removes the Oquab et al. DINOv2 and Adobe Stock references. The photometric-stereo taxonomy and principal research positioning remain. Citation-style changes, duplicate consolidation, and replacing the PS-FCN repository citation with its already-cited paper do not constitute new related work.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method overview, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten around two challenges and consistently named components. Ablation and comparison subsections are reorganized, appendix sections are restructured, and ethics, reproducibility, and LLM-use statements are introduced. This is substantial editorial reorganization beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: V3 redraws the architecture diagram and lighting-attention display, changes Figure 1's chart and comparator columns, restructures the ablation tables, and adds capacity/timing and PBR displays. The high-resolution comparison is redesigned, several example panels disappear, and DiLiGenT102 moves to the appendix. Conference formatting and extensive figure/table repositioning materially change the presentation.

improvement.justification: Clearer method exposition, the added PS-Mix comparison against UniMS-PS, and model-size controls strengthen assessment of architectural merit (Tables 3 and 6). The documented PBR extension adds useful evidence of broader applicability. However, removing sparse-input and per-complexity results weakens support for those aspects, while omitting initialization and training-subset details reduces reproducibility. These tradeoffs limit the net quality gain to a modest improvement.
